descriptionHtml:
Approach · TC-25 Web & Phone Sync · S26 Existing specs: a signed-out browser gets the sign-in gate on every clinical route (anonymous project)

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • T1 Each device goes through its own email-code sign-in (a new device always asks for a code). The two do not share a session token, and both stay valid at once. (TFA-94513 AC 6; TFA-94513 AC 10; UAT TC-25 step 1) — gate: blocked: TFA-94513 in progress

Test design technique: Error guessing (error-guessing) — Go straight for the places most likely to break (failures, double clicks, two tabs, a wrong clock, injected instructions).

Given A signed-out browser with empty storage (anonymous project)

When Open / and each clinical route directly, a chart's address included

Then Every route shows the sign-in gate, never the app: a new device always has to ask for a code

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Playwright assertions in e2e/auth.anon.spec.ts, judged against T1's 'a new device always asks for a code' (TFA-94513 AC 6). Static evidence: a generic signed-out browser, not the computer opening the phone's chart while the phone is signed in (that is S13 cp0)

Where it ran: local newspec-c (new Playwright specs); test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: existing tests (Tim's Playwright) (blocked)

S26 is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-25.matrix.json), not a step number of the UAT document.

Environment: local — main e02167f, local stack (not a deployed build); run folder runs/2026-10-14-local, lane newspec-c.

Test method: PW · Playwright script — as classified in cases/test-methods.json, which says it runs on both; Source: newspec-c.

UAT item: TC-25 Web & Phone Sync · Section: A5 · Cross-Cutting · Scenario: TC-25/S26

Existing specs: a signed-out browser gets the sign-in gate on every clinical route (anonymous project)

Tickets: TFA-94513 Signing In & Session Security (in progress)

New local lane newspec-c: status passed in newspec-c/results.json → passed (passed).

How it is tested (newspec-c/plan.json, automatable: yes): Tim's two tests in e2e/auth.anon.spec.ts (anonymous project) for /rounding, /clinic, /snf, /rounding/sheet, /settings, plus our own spec tc25-anon-routes.spec.ts (runner qa-spec) for '/', a real Hospital and Nursing Home chart address and the other clinical routes: the scenario's when names '/' and a chart's address, which Tim's titles do not open. Both halves are in the patch. — Tim's tests exist on main (anonymous project); our complement covers what they do not open.

Detail:

Tim's two anonymous-project tests pass on the local stack (2/2, runs/2026-10-14-local/newspec-c/tc25-s26.json); they open /rounding, /clinic, /snf, /rounding/sheet, /settings. Our complement (tc25-anon-routes.spec.ts) opens '/', a real Hospital chart and a real Nursing Home chart address, both dashboards, add, tasks, handoff and /handoffs: 15/15 show the sign-in form and no chart content. The patch now wires both halves (Tim's titles + our title with runner qa-spec); without ours the scenario's '/' and chart-address routes would not be covered.

Evidence: 3 attached.

Dev run: skipped: local-only — local-only — Lane A (Tim's spec e2e/auth.anon.spec.ts, anonymous project): spec-matrix.mjs runs Tim's specs against the local stack only (E2E_PORT 6473) and has no dev target, so it runs on the local stack only, once spec-matrix passes --project=anonymous (Quinn 2026-10-14).. This local result replaces that dev entry (the scenario appears once).
